review_scope: Workspace root and job path security
Claim generation/token fencing and two-reconciler races
Crash/restart, retry-error, ENOSPC and commit-uncertainty semantics
Preservation of G4 accepted DRAFT/command/outbox and original AT-21 scope

findings.detail: The supplemental contract fixes settings bounds, worker argv/stdin/result/exit DTO, filesystem root/open policy, exact layout and marker bytes/mode, no-follow traversal, marker staging/link publication, operation ordering, fixed errors, DB claim/complete/failure/retry transitions, expiry equality, crash recovery cases and named fault hooks. A TC can assert outputs and durable DB/FS states without reading production logic to generate its oracle.

The contract explicitly preserves the high-risk root-preflight rule: an unsafe/unavailable global root fails with null job_id before claiming any intent, so intents remain unchanged and are not marked ERROR. An orphan UUID directory with no intent is ignored and preserved; there is no nonexistent row to mark ERROR. Tests can independently assert these cases.

The DB claim is committed before filesystem operations; completion and failure lock the row then use a separate conditional update bound to job, generation, token and live lease. A stale reconciler may only perform stable create-once layout work and invocation-owned temporary cleanup; it may not commit state, replace a marker, or delete unknown data. The expiry comparison and acknowledgement ambiguity have fixed observable behavior.

The contract distinguishes active claims, expired claims, ERROR retry, READY no-op and unknown remnants. Empty same-intent directories may be resumed; unexpected entries are preserved and become unsafe. It does not authorize recursive deletion, implicit adoption, chmod repair or job workflow advancement.

Filesystem error mappings, ENOSPC/EDQUOT handling, subprocess command DTOs, signal shutdown, modes, marker exact bytes, private evidence and controlled-fault limitations are specified sufficiently for local real-PG/real-FS tests. The contract expressly disclaims physical power-loss, production NFS/mount, and real storage-capacity proof.

The original AT-21 workspace slice is retained while job/log/image/device endpoint isolation, B03/Temporal execution, actual Agent single-writer/worktree enforcement and production storage approval remain out of scope. G5 cannot be reported as full AT-21 completion.

fixed_independent_oracles: Exact canonical worker request/result bytes, fixed status/error codes and exit classes
Exact marker JSON bytes plus one LF, file mode 0600, directory modes 0700, UUID path containment and no-follow identity checks
Real PostgreSQL intent state, generation/token equality flags, claim-expiry boundaries, G4 job/command/outbox immutability
Operation ordering across write/fsync/close/link/child-directory sync/job sync/root sync and READY commit
Fresh-connection recovery and idempotency at every crash-table boundary
Independent process contention, stale-worker fencing, no-follow adversarial trees, sentinel preservation and explicit ENOSPC injection
required_test_layers: Unit tests for canonical settings/DTO/error mapping without treating them as filesystem acceptance
Real temporary POSIX filesystem tests for modes, symlinks, type/identity, exact bytes and preserving unknown contents
Real isolated PostgreSQL tests for claim/fence/conditional completion and G4 accepted-group immutability
Independent worker processes with bounded private logs for crash, lease race, restart and signal shutdown
Full fixed G5 candidate gate plus required G4/G1-G3/B01 regressions after source freeze
testability_assessment.nonblocking_note: Settings.workspace_root=None is described as disabling workspace operations, while a worker configured without a root is invalid_request. The implementation may expose a service-level no-op result for the disabled setting, but that return shape is not separately pinned. TC should assert that disabled mode performs no claim/FS/task work and that the CLI rejects a missing configured root; it should not invent a service return DTO unless the product API publishes one. This does not block the approved worker/API integration or G5 persistence oracles.

original_scope_guard.statement: A G5 pass is local workspace provisioning/recovery evidence only. AT-21 remains incomplete until actual job, log, image, device, file-path and session isolation are verified through their real resources; G5 does not grant deployment, execution or production-storage approval.
